acceptance_criteria.criterion: The orchestrator resolves models using the priority chain: assignments > per-persona YAML > shared YAML default
When a persona's resolved assignment slug is `"inherit"`, the orchestrator skips the assignment and falls back to YAML-based resolution
When `assignments.json` is absent, the orchestrator continues with YAML-only behavior (identical to current behavior)
Partial assignments override only the specified personas — unspecified personas fall back to YAML
When a persona's resolved assignment slug is "inherit", the orchestrator skips the assignment and falls back to YAML-based resolution

summary: Extended extract_persona_model_slugs() in orchestrator/src/utils/persona_models.py with a four-layer model resolution priority chain: per-persona assignment UUID > per-persona YAML model_slug > default_model_uuid assignment > _shared.yaml default_model_slug.

Added two new module-level helpers: _read_uuid_to_slug_map() reads personas/model-registry/local.json and returns a UUID→slug dict (empty on missing/invalid file); _read_assignments() reads assignments.json and returns the parsed dict (None on missing/invalid file). Both degrade gracefully.

The 'inherit' sentinel slug is detected after UUID resolution and causes the orchestrator to skip that assignment layer and fall through to the next — ensuring the orchestrator always resolves to a concrete model slug for API calls.

Created orchestrator/tests/test_persona_models_assignments.py with 22 pytest tests covering: assignments absent (YAML-only fallback), full override, partial assignments, inherit slug skipping, default_model_uuid override, graceful degradation on corrupt/missing files, and the full four-layer priority chain.
All 22 new tests pass. All 1132 pre-existing orchestrator tests continue to pass with no regressions.

comments.note: persona_models.py module docstring says 'returns the API-compatible model identifier for each orchestrator stage' but doesn't mention the new assignments layer. Consider updating it to document the full priority chain when the module docstring is next edited.

The glob pattern '[1-9]-*.yaml' in find_ledger_yaml_for_stage() (and the same pattern in extract_persona_model_slugs() via find_ledger_yaml_for_stage) only matches single-digit role numbers. A pre-existing comment in the file already flags this. The WP-004 implementation doesn't change this limitation, but it is worth revisiting if the number of ledger personas ever exceeds 9.

find_ledger_yaml_for_stage() re-reads workflow-manifest.json from disk on every call. extract_persona_model_slugs() calls it in a per-stage loop, causing N manifest reads per invocation. This is pre-existing behavior and not introduced by WP-004, but as the number of personas grows this will accumulate I/O. A cached manifest (read once and passed as a parameter or closure) would eliminate the redundancy — worth considering when the function is next refactored.

[documentation-forward] extract_persona_model_slugs() has a detailed docstring with its own priority chain description. Now that the module docstring also carries the authoritative narrative, the function-level docstring should cross-reference it (e.g. 'See module docstring for the full priority-chain description') rather than maintain a parallel copy. Keeping both in sync over time is a maintenance risk.

Priority chain line 380: `model_slug = assignment_slug or yaml_slug or effective_default` relies on Python truthiness — an empty string from any layer is silently skipped. This is correct behavior (empty slug is never valid) but is implicit. A future contributor who sees a YAML file with `model_slug: ''` might expect it to take effect. A comment on that line explaining the intentional empty-string skip would make this contract explicit.
